title: Boot IR0
subtitle: ISO → kernel → runit → login shell
what_you_see: QEMU or bare metal shows boot messages, then runit stages, then a login prompt or first-boot wizard on the framebuffer.
why_it_matters: Boot is the contract between firmware, kernel, and PID 1. IR0 uses a userspace-init ISO path: kernel brings up MM lazily, mounts root from disk, execs /sbin/init (runit-init).

steps.label: Firmware / GRUB
steps.image_alt: IR0 first boot on the framebuffer
steps.what_ir0_does: Multiboot or ISO boot loads kernel-x64-userspace.bin. Serial and framebuffer consoles come online.
steps.why_it_matters: Smokes assume this entry — Atlas traces start after init is scheduled.

steps.label: Kernel init
steps.what_ir0_does: Subsystems register: MM, scheduler, VFS, devfs, drivers. klog and smokes tag milestones.
steps.why_it_matters: Order matters — devfs before init opens /dev/console.

steps.label: exec /sbin/init
steps.what_ir0_does: First userspace process. On ISD this is runit-init, not a debug harness.
steps.why_it_matters: PID 1 owns reaping orphans and driving shutdown.

steps.label: runit stages
steps.what_ir0_does: /etc/runit/1 → stage 2 → getty or first-boot services. RUNIT_STAGE2_OK is the smoke gate.
steps.why_it_matters: Product shape vs one-shot test init.

steps.label: Login shell
steps.what_ir0_does: getty → ash after first-boot account creation or existing passwd.
steps.why_it_matters: The machine is now “yours” — everything in Explore IR0 assumes this point.
